summary: Iter15 — admin bulk-CSV seller import. Backend pytest 15/15 PASS (3-row happy path, mixed valid+invalid+duplicate, missing header, empty 400, oversized 413, non-admin 403, unauth 401, case-insensitive headers, created-visible-in-list, plus iter14 regression: single POST, GET list, PATCH, resend-link, set-password-with-token). Smoke + ledger e2e PASS. Frontend bulk-import modal flow VERIFIED on /admin/sellers desktop: admin-bulk-import-btn opens bulk-import-modal; bulk-import-sample-btn populates 217-char sample; bulk-import-submit posts 2-row CSV → bulk-import-result shows created=2 failed=0; bulk-import-file-input uploads real .csv File and populates the textarea via file.text() (verified 'TEST_iter15_uifile,07xxxxxx' appears); bulk-import-done-btn closes modal and refreshes list (rows 26→27). Anonymous correctly sees the 'Sign in as admin' fallback (no bulk-import button visible). HOWEVER: the entire admin UI is gated by user.role==='admin', but the backend POST /api/auth/login response object omits a 'role' field, so a real admin who logs in via the UI ends up with user.role===undefined in the zustand store and is permanently shown 'Sign in as admin' on /admin/sellers — the bulk-import button (and Register seller button) are unreachable in production via the UI. The frontend test only proceeded by patching localStorage manually. This is a HIGH-priority regression introduced before iter15 (contradicts iter14's claim that admin UI worked) but blocks the new feature delivered in iter15.

critical.issue: Response payload omits the user's 'role' field. The seed admin (seed_seller_biz_salama) has role='admin' in MongoDB but it's not surfaced in the login response, breaking every admin-only frontend gate (AdminSellersPage.tsx line 67: `user?.role !== 'admin'`). Fix: add `"role": user.get('role', 'user'),` to the login response dict at server.py:773-787.

minor.issue: STILL 500s for the seed admin because doc lacks 'auth_type' (carried over from iter14). Fix: user.get('auth_type','password').
search param not re.escape'd (carried over from iter14).

integration_issues.issue: After successful login as admin (+255700000001/AdminPass123!), the page renders the 'Sign in as admin' fallback because login response omits role. The new admin-bulk-import-btn is therefore unreachable for the real admin. Bug is in backend response, but it blocks the iter15 deliverable end-to-end via UI.

action_items: (HIGH) Add `"role": user.get('role', 'user')` to the POST /api/auth/login response dict in server.py (lines 773-787). Without this, no real admin can reach /admin/sellers via the UI, so the bulk-import modal is unreachable in production. After fix, retest /admin/sellers as +255700000001/AdminPass123! and confirm admin-bulk-import-btn renders without manual localStorage patching.
(LOW) Carry-over iter14: fix /auth/me KeyError on missing auth_type, and re.escape on admin_sellers search.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:773-787 — login response shape diverges from what the React store needs (role missing). Either return the full sanitized user doc (minus password_hash, _id) or explicitly add 'role'. Currently every admin-only UI gate is broken for real admins.

admin_sellers.py:357 (parse_bulk_csv) — row_n is stored as a string ('2','3',...) so the JSON errors[] returns {"row":"2",...} for per-row errors but {"row":0,...} for the parse-error path. Inconsistent type (str vs int) will trip downstream consumers. Coerce to int.

admin_sellers.py:413 — broad `except Exception as e` swallows programming errors (TypeError, AttributeError) into a per-row 'error' string. Keep the catch for LookupError/ValueError and let unexpected exceptions bubble so a 500 is observable.

server.py:5940 — `if not payload.csv_text or not payload.csv_text.strip()` raises 400 'csv_text is empty' which is correct, but the 413 cap is checked AFTER the strip — a 256KB payload of all whitespace would 413 instead of 400. Re-order: check size first, then emptiness.

AdminSellersPage.tsx BulkImportModal: the sample populates textarea but there's no visible CSV header validation client-side. Users will see 'Missing required column(s)' only after submitting. Consider a quick client-side header check before POSTing.

AdminSellersPage.tsx BulkImportModal: per-row errors are rendered in the result panel — confirm errors list has a data-testid for individual error rows so future automated tests can introspect (currently only [data-testid='bulk-import-result'] + counts are testable).
server.py is now > 6000 lines; admin-sellers routes should be moved to /app/backend/routes/admin_sellers.py.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of new bulk-import flow testids reachable AFTER manual role patch; 0% reachable for real admin via vanilla login flow due to login-response role-missing bug

seed_data_creation: Backend test creates ~7 TEST_iter15_* seller users via bulk endpoint (3 from happy path, 2 from mixed, 1 from case-insensitive, 1 from regression single-POST) + 1 from set-password-with-token regression (password rotated to NewPass123!). Frontend test created 3 additional TEST_iter15_ui_* sellers (2 from CSV paste, 1 from file upload). Total ~10 TEST_iter15_* docs in users collection. No cleanup performed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iter15_bulk_csv.py -v. Random phone generator uses 0712+6 digits (10 total) to match TZ format — DO NOT use 7 random digits, normalize_tz_phone rejects 11-digit strings. GET /api/admin/sellers returns {count, sellers:[...]} (a dict) not a list. The whole admin UI is currently blocked unless you patch localStorage 'biz-salama-auth' .state.user.role='admin' after login — the proper fix is one line in server.py login response.
rca of the issue: Root cause: server.py POST /api/auth/login (lines 773-787) explicitly constructs a sanitized response dict that lists individual user fields but forgot to include 'role'. AdminSellersPage.tsx gates on `user?.role !== 'admin'` so the admin UI is inaccessible. Reproduction: login as +255700000001/AdminPass123! via UI → go to /admin/sellers → see 'Sign in as admin' card despite being logged in. Mitigation: add `"role": user.get('role'),` (or full sanitized user via {**user, '_id': None, 'password_hash': None}) to the login return dict; existing zustand User type already declares role?:string.
